name: Garret Yount
abstract_title: INVESTIGATING REMOTE ELECTROGASTROGRAM MODULATION VIA EMOTIONAL AND EATING STIMULI: A SHAM-CONTROLLED PILOT STUDY
abstract: Background: Gut feelings are often described as intuitive insights with visceral origins, closely tied to emotions and, in some accounts, linked to extrasensory perception. Prior research reported changes in gut activity corresponding to a distant partner’s exposure to emotional stimuli, suggesting a potential pathway for nonlocal emotional resonance. authors: Garret Yount, Arnaud Delorme, Helané Wahbeh, Jessica Lopez, Sitara Taddeo, Michael Kriegsman, Salma Ahmadzai, Richard Tian, Dean Radin
field: Biofield science, molecular neurobiology, distant healing
notable: First NIH R01 grant to study qigong/biofield (1997); PhD in molecular neurobiology; author of 'Why Vibes Matter'
notes: Focuses on laboratory-based models of exceptional human abilities.
